items.stem: Find the class-marks of the classes 10-25 and 35-55.
items.answer: The class mark is the average of the two class limits. For 10−25 the class mark is (10 + 25)/2 = 35/2 = 17.5, and for 35−55 it is (35 + 55)/2 = 90/2 = 45. Hence the class marks are 17.5 and 45.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 OD Standard
items.ocr: The printed stem reads "35-66", but the worked solution computes the class mark of 35−55 and gets 45. Per the solution-wins rule the stem is recorded as 35-55; counted as a contradicted key.

items.stem: If the mean of the first n natural number is 15, then find n.
items.answer: The first n natural numbers are 1, 2, 3, …, n and their sum is Sₙ = n(n + 1)/2. So the mean is M = n(n + 1)/(2n) = (n + 1)/2. Setting (n + 1)/2 = 15 gives n + 1 = 30, hence n = 29.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 Delhi Standard

items.stem: What is abscissa of the point of intersection of the “Less than type” and of the “More than type” cumulative frequency curve of a grouped data ?
items.answer: The two ogives are drawn on the same axes; the “less than” curve rises and the “more than” curve falls, and they cross where exactly half the observations lie on either side. The x-coordinate of that crossing point is therefore the median of the grouped data.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS

items.stem: The median and mode respectively of a frequency distribution are 26 and 29, find its mean.
items.answer: Use the empirical relation Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M. Substituting Mₒ = 29 and M_d = 26 gives 29 = 3 × 26 − 2M, so 2M = 78 − 29 = 49 and M = 49/2 = 24.5. The mean is 24.5.
items.concept: Empirical relation of the three measures
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board 2020 Delhi Basic

items.stem: In a frequency distribution, the mid value of a class is 10 and the width of the class is 6. What is the lower limit of the class?
items.answer: Let x be the upper limit and y the lower limit. The mid value gives (x + y)/2 = 10, so x + y = 20. The width gives x − y = 6. Adding and subtracting these, x = 13 and y = 7. Hence the lower limit of the class is 7.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2014

items.stem: For finding the popular size of readymade garments, which central tendency is used?
items.answer: The “popular” size is the size that occurs most often among the buyers, which is exactly what the mode measures. Hence mode is the measure of central tendency used.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 OD 2012

items.stem: If the difference of mode and median of a data is 24, then what is the difference of median and mean?
items.answer: We are given Mₒ − M_d = 24, and the empirical relation is Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M. Substituting, Mₒ − M_d = 3M_d − 2M − M_d = 2(M_d − M), so 24 = 2(M_d − M). Hence M_d − M = 12, i.e. the difference of median and mean is 12.
items.concept: Empirical relation of the three measures
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 OD 2011

items.stem: The median of a set of 9 distinct observations is 20.5. If each of the largest 4 observation of the set is increased by 2, then what is the median of the new set?
items.answer: With n = 9 the median is the ((9 + 1)/2)ᵗʰ = 5ᵗʰ observation in ascending order. Increasing the largest four observations by 2 changes only the top four values; their order is preserved and the 5ᵗʰ observation is untouched. Hence the median is unchanged and remains 20.5.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 OD 2013

items.stem: If the mean of the observation x, x + 3, x + 5, x + 7 and x + 10 is 9, the find the mean of the last three observation
items.answer: The mean of the five observations is (x + x + 3 + x + 5 + x + 7 + x + 10)/5 = (5x + 25)/5 = 9, so 5x + 25 = 45 and x = 4. The last three observations are x + 5, x + 7 and x + 10, whose sum is 3x + 22 = 12 + 22 = 34. Their mean is 34/3 = 11⅓.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 OD 2014
items.ocr: The solution misprints the sum of the last three as (5x + 22)/3 in one line, then correctly uses (3x + 22)/3 = 34/3 in the next; the final result 11⅓ is right.

items.stem: A set of numbers consists of three 4’s, five 5’s, six 6’s, eight 8’s and seven 10’s. What is the mode of this set of numbers?
items.answer: The mode is the value with the highest frequency. The frequencies are 4 → 3 times, 5 → 5 times, 6 → 6 times, 8 → 8 times and 10 → 7 times. The largest frequency is 8, belonging to the value 8. Hence the mode is 8.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2012

items.stem: The mean weight of 9 students is 25 kg. If one more student is joined in the group the mean is unaltered, then find the weight of the 10ᵗʰ student.
items.answer: The total weight of the 9 students is 25 × 9 = 225 kg. After the tenth student joins, the mean is still 25 kg for 10 students, so the new total is 25 × 10 = 250 kg. The tenth student therefore weighs 250 − 225 = 25 kg. (Equivalently: if adding an observation leaves the mean unchanged, that observation must equal the mean.)
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2013

items.stem: The mean and median of the data a, b and c are 50 and 35 respectively, where a < b < c. If c − a = 55, then find the value of (b − a).
items.answer: Since a < b < c, the middle value b is the median, so b = 35. From the mean, (a + b + c)/3 = 50 gives a + b + c = 150, hence a + c = 150 − 35 = 115. Together with c − a = 55, subtracting gives 2a = 60, so a = 30. Therefore b − a = 35 − 30 = 5.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 OD 2014

items.stem: If the mean of the squares of first n natural numbers is 105, then find the first n natural numbers.
items.answer: The sum of the squares of the first n natural numbers is Σx² = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6, so their mean is (n + 1)(2n + 1)/6. Setting (n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 = 105 gives 2n² + 3n + 1 = 630, i.e. 2n² + 3n − 629 = 0. Factorising, (2n + 37)(n − 17) = 0, and since n must be positive, n = 17. The numbers are 1, 2, 3, …, 17.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2011

items.stem: Observations of some data are x/5, x, x/3, 2x/3, x/4, 2x/5 and 3x/4 where x > 0. If the median of the data is 4, then what is the value of x?
items.answer: Arranging the seven observations in ascending order gives x/5, x/4, x/3, 2x/5, 2x/3, 3x/4, x. With n = 7 (odd), the median is the ((7 + 1)/2)ᵗʰ = 4ᵗʰ observation, which is 2x/5. Setting 2x/5 = 4 gives x = (4 × 5)/2 = 10.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2013

items.stem: If the coordinates of the point of intersection of less than ogive and more than ogive is (13.5, 20), then find the value of median.
items.answer: The abscissa (x-coordinate) of the point where the two ogives cross is the median of the data. Here that abscissa is 13.5, so the median is 13.5.

items.answer: The largest frequency is 23, so the modal class is 12-15. Here l = 12, h = 3, f₁ = 23, f₀ = 10 and f₂ = 21. Then Mₒ = l + (f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂) × h = 12 + (23 − 10)/(46 − 10 − 21) × 3 = 12 + (13/15) × 3 = 12 + 13/5 = 14.6. The mode is 14.6.

items.stem: What is abscissa of the point of intersection of the “Less than type” and of the “More than type” cumulative frequency curve of a grouped data ?
items.answer: The “less than” and “more than” ogives intersect at the point where half the total frequency lies on either side. The abscissa of that point of intersection is the median of the grouped data.

items.stem: If median is 137 and mean is 137.05, then what is the value of mode ?
items.answer: By the empirical relation Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M = 3(137) − 2(137.05) = 411 − 274.10 = 136.90. The mode is 136.90.

items.answer: The expenditure done by the maximum number of workers is the mode. The largest frequency is 40, so the modal class is 1500-2000, with l = 1500, h = 500, f₁ = 40, f₀ = 24 and f₂ = 33. Then Mₒ = 1500 + (40 − 24)/(80 − 24 − 33) × 500 = 1500 + (16/23) × 500 = 1500 + 347.83 = ₹1847.83 (approximately).

items.stem: If xᵢ’s are the mid-points of the class intervals of grouped data, fᵢ’s are the corresponding frequencies and x̄ is the mean, then find Σ(fᵢxᵢ − x̄).
items.answer: Expand the sum: Σ(fᵢxᵢ − x̄) = Σfᵢxᵢ − Σx̄ = Σfᵢxᵢ − nx̄. Since x̄ = (Σfᵢxᵢ)/n, we have nx̄ = Σfᵢxᵢ, so the expression becomes Σfᵢxᵢ − Σfᵢxᵢ = 0. Hence Σ(fᵢxᵢ − x̄) = 0.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 Delhi 2017

items.stem: Which central tendency is obtained by the abscissa of point of intersection of less than type and more than type ogives ?
items.answer: The x-coordinate of the point where the “less than” and “more than” ogives meet corresponds to the value below and above which half the observations lie. That central tendency is the median.

items.stem: If the median of a series exceeds the mean by 3, find by what number the mode exceeds its mean?
items.answer: We are given M_d = M + 3. By the empirical relation, Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M = 3(M + 3) − 2M = 3M + 9 − 2M = M + 9. Hence the mode exceeds the mean by 9.
items.concept: Empirical relation of the three measures

items.stem: Find median of the data, using an empirical relation when it is given that Mode = 12.4 and Mean = 10.5.
items.answer: The empirical relation Mₒ = 3M_d − 2M rearranges to M_d = (Mₒ + 2M)/3 = ⅓Mₒ + ⅔M. Substituting, M_d = ⅓(12.4) + ⅔(10.5) = 12.4/3 + 21/3 = 33.4/3 = 11.13 (approximately). The median is 11.13.
items.concept: Empirical relation of the three measures

items.stem: Find the mean of the data using an empirical formula when it is given that mode is 50.5 and median in 45.5.
items.answer: Write the empirical relation as 3M_d = Mₒ + 2M. Substituting M_d = 45.5 and Mₒ = 50.5 gives 3 × 45.5 = 50.5 + 2M, so 136.5 − 50.5 = 2M and M = 86/2 = 43. The mean is 43.
items.concept: Empirical relation of the three measures

items.stem: Find the mean of first odd multiples of 5.
items.answer: The first five odd multiples of 5 are 5, 15, 25, 35 and 45. Their sum is 5 + 15 + 25 + 35 + 45 = 125, and there are 5 of them, so the mean is 125/5 = 25.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-1 2012
